sources.entry: DisableMonitor - Easily disable or enable a monitor on your Mac.

summary.one_liner: DisableMonitor is a macOS utility that disables, enables, or changes the resolution of an attached display, with a command-line interface.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a macOS app that turns a connected monitor off or on and can change its resolution. A console mode lists attached monitors with their IDs (--list), and accepts --disable ID and --enable ID to toggle a specific display. The changelog mentions moving windows from a disabled monitor to an active one, disabling mirrored monitors, a resolution manager with aspect ratio options, lock-screen and screensaver menu items, and an automatic update check. The README also mentions "Rules" in version 1.9 marked as BETA, without describing how they work. The project is described as having stopped development.
use_cases: turn off a secondary monitor on a Mac
list monitor IDs from the terminal
script enabling or disabling a display
move windows off a disconnected monitor
stack: Objective-C/macOS (inferred from OSX framework build requirement)
notable: Console switches to list, disable, and enable monitors by ID
Can move windows from a disabled monitor to an active one
Supports changing monitor resolution with aspect ratio handling
caveats: README warns the software can cause irretrievable damage to the computer; use at your own risk
Development has stopped and the project is not being continued; maintainers are sought
